# Vendored third-party readers

Code brought in from other repositories so the tool can read disk images,
acquisitions and databases without asking the examiner to install anything.
qnxprobe.py, ewfprobe.py, cimreader.py, regfprobe.py and the ccl_segb package are copied verbatim;
impacket_ese.py is adapted, as its own section below explains. The CCL LevelDB,
IndexedDB and V8 readers in ccl/ are covered in the last section.

## qnxprobe.py

| | |
| --- | --- |
| upstream | https://github.com/abrignoni/qnxprobe |
| licence | MIT, kept beside it as LICENSE-qnxprobe |

Reads QNX6, QNX4, ext2/3/4, FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, HFS+, APFS, the QNX flash
filesystems ETFS and EFS, and QNX IFS boot images out of a raw image, without
mounting and with no administrator rights. `scripts/raw_image.py` imports it and
reads an image through its `volumes()` call. Python 3 standard library only, so
vendoring it adds no dependency to requirements.txt.

## ewfprobe.py

| | |
| --- | --- |
| upstream | https://github.com/abrignoni/ewfprobe |
| licence | MIT, kept beside it as LICENSE-ewfprobe |

Reads an EnCase/EWF acquisition (`.E01` and its numbered segments) as an ordinary
seekable image. qnxprobe reaches it by name, and `scripts/raw_image.py` imports
this copy first so that the name resolves to it in a frozen build as well as from
source. Standard library only, so this adds no dependency either.

## ccl_segb/

| | |
| --- | --- |
| upstream | https://github.com/cclgroupltd/ccl-segb (the `ccl_segb` package folder) |
| licence | MIT, kept beside it as LICENSE-ccl_segb |

Reads SEGB version 1 and version 2 files, the record containers Biome streams are
kept in. `scripts/macos_biome.py` imports it. The package's five files are copied
verbatim with their relative imports, so they stay a package here. Standard
library only, so this adds no dependency.

## cimreader.py

| | |
| --- | --- |
| upstream | https://github.com/abrignoni/cimreader (renamed from cimprobe on 2026-10-31, before any release was tagged) |
| licence | Apache-2.0, kept beside it as LICENSE-cimreader, with its NOTICE as NOTICE-cimreader |

Reads the Windows WMI CIM repository (`OBJECTS.DATA`, `INDEX.BTR` and the mapping
files) and decodes namespaces, classes and instances. It is a port of python-cim
(Mandiant flare-wmi, Apache-2.0); its NOTICE names python-cim's authors and is kept
here because the licence requires it to travel with the code. The WMI Repository
artifacts in `scripts/artifacts/windowsWmiRepository.py` import it. Standard library
only, so this adds no dependency.

## regfprobe.py

| | |
| --- | --- |
| upstream | https://github.com/abrignoni/regfprobe |
| licence | MIT, kept beside it as LICENSE-regfprobe |

Reads Windows registry hives (regf) offline, and replays their `.LOG1` and `.LOG2`
transaction logs in memory. Its log replay was copied from `scripts/registry_recovery.py`,
which now imports it from here. The registry artifacts read hives with it, through the
python-registry shaped `Registry` in `scripts/windows_registry.py`, and the vendored dpapiprobe
reads the SYSTEM and SECURITY hives with it. Standard library
only, so this adds no dependency. The upstream window, `regfprobe_gui.py`, is not copied.

## impacket_ese.py

| | |
| --- | --- |
| upstream | https://github.com/fortra/impacket, tag impacket_0_13_1, commit c456746d7a0f0bb25e8968a59f25aae1ad519935 (2026-05-15) |
| licence | Apache Software License (Impacket's modified form), kept beside it as LICENSE-impacket |

Reads an ESE (Extensible Storage Engine, `.edb`) database, used by the SRUM
artifacts to read `SRUDB.dat`. Unlike the two files above, this one is **adapted,
not copied verbatim**: impacket's `impacket/structure.py` and `impacket/ese.py`
are folded into one self-contained file, and their impacket, six and logging
imports are replaced with small inline shims, so the reader needs nothing outside
the Python standard library. No line of the parsing bodies is changed; only the
import lines were removed and the shims added. It was checked to decode a real
`SRUDB.dat` byte for byte identically to upstream impacket 0.13.1, on Python 3.10
and 3.14.

Because it is adapted rather than verbatim it is **not** listed in `vendored.json`:
`check_vendored.py` requires a tracked file to match its upstream byte for byte,
which an adapted file cannot. To update it, re-adapt from the impacket source at
the tag above. It is regenerated by stripping the import lines from the two
upstream files (verified byte-identical to the tag) and prepending the shim block.

The vendored version, upstream commit and sha256 of qnxprobe.py, ewfprobe.py,
cimreader.py and the ccl_segb files are recorded in `vendored.json` in this directory, which
`admin/scripts/check_vendored.py` enforces in CI: it checks the hashes and fetches
each upstream file at its recorded commit. They are deliberately not repeated here,
because prose is checked by nobody and the manifest is checked on every push.

**qnxprobe.py, ewfprobe.py and cimreader.py are copied verbatim. Do not edit them here.** Fix
upstream, then re-vendor, or the next sync silently reverts the change.

### Re-vendoring

    cp ../qnxprobe/qnxprobe.py scripts/vendor/qnxprobe.py
    cp ../qnxprobe/ewfprobe.py scripts/vendor/ewfprobe.py
    cp ../cimreader/cimreader.py scripts/vendor/cimreader.py
    python3 admin/scripts/check_vendored.py --update

`--update` rewrites the hashes only. The upstream commit and date in
`vendored.json` are what say which version this is, so set those by hand from
`git -C ../qnxprobe log -1 --format='%H %cI' main` (ewfprobe's come from
qnxprobe's own `vendored.json`, since the copy here is the one qnxprobe carries).
Then run the check without `--update`, which fetches the upstream file at the
commit you recorded and fails if the copy is not that file.

### Checking for drift

`admin/scripts/check_vendored.py` compares each copy against the sha256 recorded
in `vendored.json` and against the upstream file at the recorded commit, and
fails when either differs. It runs in CI, so a local edit or a stale copy after an
upstream release is caught rather than noticed later. Pass `--upstream <path>`
(or `--upstream qnxprobe=<path>`) to compare against a checkout instead of
fetching, and `--offline` to check the hashes alone.

## ccl/ (CCL Forensics LevelDB, IndexedDB and V8 readers)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| upstream | https://github.com/cclgroupltd/ccl_chromium_reader and https://github.com/cclgroupltd/ccl_simplesnappy |
| licence | MIT, kept here as LICENSE-ccl_chromium_reader and LICENSE-ccl_simplesnappy |

The Chromium, Discord, Slack, Wire, Roblox, WhatsApp Web and webOS readers import these
from `scripts.vendor.ccl`. Upstream keeps them in a package
(`ccl_chromium_reader`, with `storage_formats` and `serialization_formats` subfolders)
whose `__init__` imports modules DLEAPP does not use and a `zstd` package it does not
depend on, so they are kept here as one flat folder with an `__init__.py` of this
repository's.

Verbatim copies, recorded in vendored.json:

- `ccl_v8_value_deserializer.py`: ccl_chromium_reader 3be9221 (2024-06-12), unchanged
  upstream since.
- `ccl_blink_value_deserializer.py`, `common.py` and `profile_folder_protocols.py`:
  ccl_chromium_reader ad37443 (2026-10-28).
- `ccl_simplesnappy.py`: ccl_simplesnappy 2161c40 (2024-07-29). That commit carried no
  LICENSE file; the MIT text kept here is the repository's later one, and the file's
  own header holds the same licence.

Copies with local changes, not in vendored.json because it records only copies whose
body equals upstream:

- `ccl_chromium_indexeddb.py` and `structures.py`: ccl_chromium_reader ad37443, with
  only their imports changed for the flat folder (`from . import ccl_leveldb`,
  `from . import ccl_simplesnappy` and the like).
- `ccl_leveldb.py`: ccl_chromium_reader ad37443 with DLEAPP 051660d merged in, and
  `import ccl_simplesnappy` changed to `from . import ccl_simplesnappy`. That
  change bounds the open file handles: a reader closes each .log and .ldb file after
  checking it and reopens it for each pass, and what a pass skips as damage is copied
  back to the file's reader, where upstream keeps it. Upstream ad37443 still fails
  admin/test/scripts/test_leveldb_file_lifecycle.py without it (5 of 11 tests,
  measured 2026-11-03), so it stays until upstream takes an equivalent change.

Two helpers around them stay in `scripts/ccl`: `wire_assets.py`, this repository's own code,
and `indexeddb_to_json.py`, an in-memory adaptation of Spyder Forensics' IndexedDBtoJSON.py
helper, as its header says. Before 2026-11-03 these readers sat in `scripts/ccl` too.
